mainTopic: When grape juice counts as 'wine': the בור, קיפוי and barrel stages for מעשרות, and the stricter rule for יין נסך
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא. You may not help a Jew who makes his wine in טומאה, but you may harvest grapes with a נכרי. The גמרא then quotes the משנה: a נכרי's touch does not make juice into יין נסך until it goes down into the בור (collection vat). It challenges this with a teaching about מעשרות that says wine counts only from when it 'floats' (קיפוי). רבא answers that the two sources follow different opinions: the רבנן say the בור, and רבי עקיבא says floating. The גמרא proves that this floating happens in the בור, not in the barrel. Then רב זביד's version of the dispute moves both opinions one stage later. In that version the רבנן say the בור plus floating, and רבי עקיבא says once the wine is drawn into barrels. The גמרא adopts that reading. That seems to make our משנה a third opinion. The גמרא answers that יין נסך is different, because the חכמים were extra strict about it.

steps.title: Do not help a Jew who makes his wine impure, but you may harvest with a נכרי
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא finishes its rule. One may not harvest, and certainly not tread, with a Jew who makes his produce in טומאה. One may harvest with a נכרי, because it is allowed to cause טומאה to ordinary חולין in ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you may not harvest grapes with a Jew who makes his produce in impurity, and certainly you may not tread grapes with him. But you may harvest grapes into the winepress with a נכרי, because it is permitted to cause impurity to ordinary produce in ארץ ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא about whose grape harvest you may help with. You may not help a Jew who is making his wine טמא, but you may help a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Helping a Jew who makes his wine in טומאה means helping him sin, so it is forbidden. Treading is worse than harvesting, because treading is the very step where the juice comes out and becomes טמא. With a נכרי the only issue is causing טומאה to ordinary חולין, and the ברייתא says doing that is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: harvesting (picking) grapes
treading grapes to squeeze out the juice
ritual impurity
winepress
to cause something to become impure
ordinary, non-sacred produce

steps.confusionAlert: The problem with the Jew is not his wine being forbidden to drink. The problem is that he is making his produce טמא, and you would be helping him do that.

phrases.english: And one may not harvest grapes with a Jew
who makes his produce in a state of impurity,
and all the more so one may not tread grapes with him,
but one may harvest grapes into the winepress with the gentile,
because it is permitted to cause impurity
to ordinary produce that is in Eretz Yisrael.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין בּוֹצְרִין עִם יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁעוֹשֶׂה פֵּירוֹתָיו בְּטוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes a ברייתא that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not harvest or tread with a Jew who makes his produce טמא. You may harvest with a נכרי, since causing טומאה to חולין in ארץ ישראל is allowed.

steps.title: The משנה's rule: no יין נסך until the juice reaches the vat
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. The juice does not become יין נסך until it goes down into the בור.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the נכרי's touch does not make the juice into יין נסך until it goes down into the collection vat (בור).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה to set up a question about it. This step prepares the next move.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the juice reaches the בור it does not yet count as 'wine'. So a נכרי's touch at that stage cannot make it יין נסך. The exact moment juice becomes 'wine' is what the גמרא will now examine.

keyTerms.meaning: wine forbidden because a נכרי touched it, treated like wine poured for idol worship
the collection vat below the winepress

phrases.english: And he does not make it libation wine
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. 'He' is the נכרי who is treading the grapes.

phrases.english: until it descends into the collection vat.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵינוֹ עוֹשֶׂה יֵין נֶסֶךְ עַד שֶׁיֵּרֵד לְבוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic by quoting the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נכרי's touch makes juice into יין נסך only once it reaches the בור.

steps.title: Challenge: another teaching says wine counts only from the 'floating' stage
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says wine counts as wine from when it is משיקפה, a later stage than the בור. This seems to contradict the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was taught: wine counts as wine from the time it floats!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה with a ברייתא that sets a different point for when juice becomes 'wine'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats the juice as wine as soon as it reaches the בור. The ברייתא says it is wine only once the solid bits float on top, which is a later stage. So which moment makes it 'wine'?

keyTerms.meaning: from when it floats, when the solid residue rises to the top

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא is about when you must take מעשרות from wine, not about יין נסך. The גמרא assumes both rules depend on the same thing: when the juice counts as finished wine.

phrases.english: But isn't it taught:
Wine is considered wine from when it floats!
phrases.notes: That teaching is about when you must take מעשרות. It means when the bits of seeds and skins float up to the top.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה quoted in step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that juice counts as wine once it reaches the בור.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another source sets the 'wine' stage later, at קיפוי, so the two seem to contradict.

steps.title: רבא: the two sources follow two different opinions
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that there is no contradiction. The ברייתא follows רבי עקיבא, and the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is not difficult. That teaching follows רבי עקיבא, and this one follows the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא resolves the contradiction by saying each source follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources really do disagree, so רבא does not try to make them say the same thing. He explains that they reflect a known argument: the 'floating' teaching is רבי עקיבא's view, and our משנה is the רבנן's view.

keyTerms.meaning: it is not difficult (there is no contradiction)
this one ... that one
the Sages, the majority opinion

phrases.english: Rava said: It is not difficult,
that one follows Rabbi Akiva,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the teaching about 'floating' from step 3.

phrases.english: this one follows the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is our משנה, which uses the בור stage.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא לָא קַשְׁיָא הָא רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הָא רַבָּנַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the two sources to different תנאים (מחלוקת).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to give one shared rule for when juice becomes wine, so they looked contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: They follow different opinions. The רבנן say the בור, and רבי עקיבא says קיפוי.

steps.title: The source for the argument between the רבנן and רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבא brings the teaching that shows the dispute. The רבנן say wine counts from when it goes down to the בור, and רבי עקיבא says from when it floats.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned: Wine counts from when it goes down into the vat. רבי עקיבא says: from when it floats.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא backs up his answer by quoting the teaching where this argument is actually recorded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the dispute is real and not invented to solve the problem. The first opinion, which is the רבנן, matches our משנה's בור stage. רבי עקיבא's opinion matches the 'floating' teaching.
steps.whatToRemember: There are two opinions on when juice becomes 'wine'. The רבנן say once it goes down to the בור, and רבי עקיבא says once it floats (קיפוי). At this point our משנה about יין נסך seems to follow the רבנן, but Steps 9–11 revise this picture.

phrases.english: as we learned:
Wine counts from when it descends into the vat,
Rabbi Akiva says: from when it floats.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רבא's answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: That the רבנן and רבי עקיבא argue about when juice becomes wine.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching that brings the בור view first and רבי עקיבא's קיפוי view after it.

steps.title: What 'floating' does רבי עקיבא mean: in the vat or in the barrel?
steps.stepSummary: The scholars ask whether רבי עקיבא's 'floating' means floating in the בור or floating in the barrel (חבית).
steps.simpleTranslation: A question was asked: Is it floating in the vat, or floating in the barrel?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks exactly which 'floating' רבי עקיבא means. This opens a new question that the coming lines will discuss.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Floating' could happen at two stages. One is when seeds float up in the collection vat. The other is when the yeast-foam floats up later in the storage barrel. The answer sets how late רבי עקיבא's 'wine' stage comes.

keyTerms.meaning: a question was asked of them (the scholars)
floating, when the residue rises to the top
barrel, a storage jar for wine

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Is it floating in the vat,
phrases.notes: This means the seeds and skins rising to the top in the collection vat.

phrases.english: or floating in the barrel?
phrases.notes: This means the yeast-foam rising later, once the wine is in the storage barrel.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ קִיפּוּי דְּבוֹר אוֹ קִיפּוּי דְּחָבִית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the word 'floating' in רבי עקיבא's opinion from step 5 refers to.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי עקיבא's קיפוי means floating in the בור or floating in the חבית.

steps.title: Proof that the floating happens in the pit
steps.stepSummary: The same teaching about 'floating' continues: even after the floating, wine can still be collected from the upper winepress and the pipe and drunk without taking מעשרות. So the floating must happen in the בור, not in the barrel.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: a ברייתא says that wine becomes obligated in מעשרות from when it floats. Even after it has floated, a person may still catch wine from the upper winepress and from the pipe and drink it. Learn from this that we are talking about floating in the בור. Yes, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 6. It shows that רבי עקיבא's 'floating' means floating in the בור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that after the floating, wine is still flowing in the upper winepress and the pipe. That is only possible while the wine is still being made and running into the בור. If the floating were in the barrels, all the wine would already be out of the press and the pipe.

keyTerms.meaning: Floating: the skins and seeds rise to the top of the wine.
The upper winepress, where the grapes are trodden.
The pipe that carries the juice from the press down to the בור.
Learn from it. A conclusion drawn from the source.

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
Wine: from when it floats,
phrases.notes: This means from when it becomes obligated in מעשרות. The skins and seeds float up to the top.

phrases.english: even though it has floated,
one may catch wine from the upper winepress
and from the pipe, and drink it.
Learn from it: we are speaking about floating in the pit.
Yes, learn from it.

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does 'floating' mean in the בור or in the חבית?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In the בור, because wine is still in the press and the pipe after the floating.

steps.title: A different version moves both opinions later
steps.stepSummary: רב זביד taught the dispute differently. The רבנן say the wine must go down into the בור and float. רבי עקיבא says it counts only when it is drawn into barrels.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רב זביד teach in the school of רבי אושעיא: wine counts from when it goes down into the בור and floats, and רבי עקיבא says from when it is drawn off into barrels!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the version of the dispute from Step 5 by quoting a different version of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the רבנן said 'goes down to the בור' and רבי עקיבא said 'floats'. In רב זביד's version, the רבנן say 'goes down and floats' and רבי עקיבא says 'drawn into barrels'. The two versions do not match.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he teach? Introduces a conflicting source.
The school (study hall) of רבי אושעיא.
Draws the wine out of the pit.
Barrels.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Zevid teach
in the school of Rabbi Oshaya:
Wine: from when it goes down into the pit and floats,
Rabbi Akiva says:
from when one draws it off into barrels!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָתָנֵי רַב זְבִיד בִּדְבֵי רַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the version of the dispute quoted in Step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: The version of the dispute in Step 5 (רבנן: בור; רבי עקיבא: floating).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another version of the same dispute puts both opinions one stage later, so the two versions contradict each other.

steps.title: Read the first version like רב זביד's version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says to explain the first ברייתא the same way: the רבנן say 'into the בור and floats', and רבי עקיבא says 'into barrels'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Explain that first ברייתא this way too: wine counts from when it goes down into the בור and floats, and רבי עקיבא says from when it is drawn off into barrels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by rereading the first version so that it matches רב זביד's version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of keeping two different versions, the גמרא adopts רב זביד's wording for both. Now the רבנן require going down and floating, and רבי עקיבא waits until the wine is in barrels.

keyTerms.meaning: Explain it, fix it. Reinterpret the source.
The first one (the earlier ברייתא).
Like this, in this way.

steps.confusionAlert: After this step, the floating that Step 7 proved belongs to the רבנן's opinion. רבי עקיבא now says 'barrels'.

phrases.english: Explain that first one this way too:
phrases.notes: 'That first one' is the ברייתא quoted back in Step 5.

phrases.english: Wine: from when it goes down into the pit and floats,
Rabbi Akiva says:
from when one draws it off into barrels.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text: one version is adjusted to match the other.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two versions of the dispute contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both versions are read the same way: רבנן = בור and floating; רבי עקיבא = barrels.

steps.title: Does the משנה make a third opinion?
steps.stepSummary: Now the משנה, which says 'only going down to the בור', matches neither the רבנן nor רבי עקיבא. Must we say there are three תנאים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, our משנה that teaches that a non-Jew does not make it יין נסך until it goes down into the בור: shall we say this is a third opinion, so there are three תנאים?
steps.whatsHappening: The new reading from Step 9 creates a new problem. The גמרא asks whom the משנה follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, רבא said the משנה follows the רבנן ('goes down to the בור'). Now the רבנן say 'goes down and floats', so the משנה matches no one. That would mean three opinions: going down, going down and floating, and barrels.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה.
Shall we say? Suggests a conclusion the גמרא would rather avoid.
Three תנאים, three different opinions.

phrases.english: But then, our Mishnah that teaches:
he does not make it libation wine
until it goes down into the pit
shall we say it is three Tannaim?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a new problem caused by the answer in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim in Step 4 that the משנה follows the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: After Step 9, the רבנן require floating too, so the משנה's 'only the בור' becomes an unknown third opinion.

steps.title: יין נסך is different because of extra strictness
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is not a third opinion. The חכמים in general were extra strict about יין נסך, so it applies already when the wine goes down into the בור, even before the stage that counts for מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. יין נסך is different, because the רבנן were strict about it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the קשיא. The משנה's earlier point is a special stricter rule for יין נסך, not a third opinion about when wine is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For מעשרות, the stages stay as the two sides of the dispute say. For יין נסך, the חכמים in general added a stricter rule, so the wine becomes forbidden even before the floating. So the משנה is not a third opinion about when wine is finished: for מעשרות, its תנא can hold like either רבי עקיבא or the רבנן.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different.
They were strict.
Wine poured for idol worship, which is forbidden.

steps.whatToRemember: For מעשרות: the רבנן say wine counts from going down into the בור and floating, and רבי עקיבא says from being drawn into barrels. For יין נסך, the חכמים made a stricter rule, so it applies already when the wine goes down into the בור, whichever side you follow for מעשרות.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one item can count as 'finished' at different stages for different laws, depending on how strict the רבנן were.

phrases.english: No, libation wine is different,
for the Rabbis were strict with it.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the laws: יין נסך has its own stricter rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה is a third opinion about when wine counts as wine.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה reflects the חכמים's general extra strictness for יין נסך, not a new opinion on when wine is finished. For מעשרות it can follow either רבי עקיבא or the רבנן.
